topics.title: Coursework & Written Assignments
topics.summary: CUHK delegates generative AI policy to course instructors. In Chung Chi College General Education (GECC3130/4130, AY2026/27), Approach 2 is mandated: drafting is prohibited, spelling/grammar checking is allowed (subject to Senate General Education approval), and AI Index > 25% may receive a failing course grade.
topics.scope: CUHK undergraduate and postgraduate courses; specific rules defined by course instructors and faculties.
actions: Verify course-specific AI rule in each syllabus
Do not use AI for drafting under Approach 2
Follow course instructions for acknowledging any permitted AI assistance

claims.text: GECC4130 Senior Seminar Course Outline 2026/27 | Chung Chi College, CUHK

evidence.quote:
Approach 2 (i.e. “Use only with prior permission”) is adopted for Chung Chi College General
Education courses (the revised approach is subject to approval by the Senate Committee on General Education).
Students are not allowed to use generative AI (GenAI) tools to prepare or write any part of their written assignments,
such as proposals, essays, or project reports. However, students may use GenAI tools solely for spelling and grammar
checking. In addition, students are strongly discouraged from using GenAI tools to generate summaries or paraphrases
as a substitute for close reading of the core texts. Students may also be asked to engage in interactions with GenAI tools
under teachers’ strict supervision.

topics.title: Declaration & Disclosure
topics.statusLabel: Signed Declaration in GECC4130 (Central Rule Unverified)
topics.summary: In verified courses (such as GECC4130), students must sign and submit an academic honesty declaration acknowledging awareness of AI detection (VeriGuide AWD). University-wide declaration and prompt-logging requirements remain unverified behind Student Guide SSO.
topics.scope: Coursework submissions where AI is used; verified in General Education courses.
actions: Submit signed academic honesty declaration where required by course outline (e.g. GECC4130)
Be aware that submissions may be investigated by AI content detection software (VeriGuide AWD)
Follow course instructor instructions for acknowledging any permitted AI use

claims.text: GECC4130 Senior Seminar Course Outline 2026/27 | Chung Chi College, CUHK

evidence.quote:
With each assignment, students will be required to submit a signed declaration that they are aware of these policies,
regulations, guidelines and procedures.
 For group projects of GECC4130, all students of the same group should be asked to sign the declaration, each of
whom is responsible and liable to disciplinary actions should there be any plagiarized contents in the group project,
irrespective of whether he/she has signed the declaration and whether he/she has contributed directly or indirectly to
the plagiarized contents.
 For assignments in the form of a computer-generated document that is principally text-based and submitted via
VeriGuide, the statement, in the form of a receipt, will be issued by the system upon students' uploading of the soft
copy of the assignment.
 Students are fully aware that their work may be investigated by AI content detection software to determine originality.
Assignments without the properly signed declaration will not be graded by teachers.

topics.title: Officially Endorsed Tools
topics.statusLabel: Copilot Basic/Premium, Gemini Enterprise, API Portal
topics.summary: Centrally provisioned tools include Microsoft Copilot Chat (Basic, free for all students/staff with institutional sign-in) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium, centrally allocated to eligible teaching staff and management; other units require departmental funding). CUHK AI Chatbot learning/teaching services are legacy services scheduled for retirement on 31 January 2027 for transition only. Generative AI API Portal access requires application, use-case review, and funding/quota. Perplexity Enterprise is planned but not currently available.
topics.scope: Centrally provisioned enterprise services, ITSC software, and cloud agreements.
actions: Apply for Gemini Enterprise if eligible
Migrate from legacy chatbots before Jan 2027

additionalTopics.title: Academic Integrity & Penalties
additionalTopics.statusLabel: Senate Misconduct Policy (Zero Marks to Expulsion)
additionalTopics.summary: A CUHK student may lodge a written appeal with full justifications against a first-instance disciplinary decision or recommendation made by a faculty/college disciplinary committee or FTP Committee to the Senate Committee on Student Discipline (SCSD) THROUGH the first-instance committee within 7 working days of notification under Senate procedures (effective from AY2025-26, updated July 2026). For disciplinary cases handled directly by the Senate Committee on Student Discipline (such as exceptionally serious cases or recommended penalties lower than guidelines), students may lodge a written appeal with full justifications DIRECTLY to the Senate Committee on Student Discipline within 7 working days of notification under Senate procedures (effective from AY2025-26, updated July 2026).
additionalTopics.scope: First-instance faculty/college or FTP route versus cases handled directly by SCSD.
actions: Submit full written reasons within 7 working days of notification.
Use the first-instance committee forwarding route unless the original case was handled directly by SCSD.

claims.text: A CUHK student may lodge a written appeal with full justifications against a first-instance disciplinary decision or recommendation made by a faculty/college disciplinary committee or FTP Committee to the Senate Committee on Student Discipline (SCSD) THROUGH the first-instance committee within 7 working days of notification under Senate procedures (effective from AY2025-26, updated July 2026).

evidence.quote: Appeals in writing with full justifications may be lodged to the Senate Committee on Student Discipline through the disciplinary committee/the FTP Committee that deals with the case in the first instance, against the decision/recommendation made by the disciplinary committee/the FTP Committee, within seven working days after the student has received the notification. The appeal shall be handled in accordance with the “Procedures for Handling Student Disciplinary Cases” of the Senate Committee on Student Discipline. Late appeals shall not be considered. The case is closed if no appeal is received after the specified period.
